activities.caption: find the faulty line — the busy-stillness summary
activities.name: eqTrafficSpot

config.prompt: A summary of dynamic equilibrium contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Two conditions define it: a closed system, and equal forward and reverse rates.
At the balance point, molecules are still colliding and reacting billions of times per second.
Every forward event is matched by a reverse one — like a store where customers enter exactly as fast as they leave.
Radioactive tracer atoms stop moving at equilibrium, proving the mixture has finally come to rest.
Open reactions never reach it: products leave, so nothing can settle.
config.correction: Tracer atoms keep swapping between reactants and products even though concentrations never budge — the movement never stops.
config.why: It is motion in balance, not stillness — the busiest stillness in science.

activities.anchor: the equilibrium position is the colour
activities.caption: drag the divider across the sealed NO₂ tube
activities.name: eqTubeCompare

config.prompt: The brown ⇌ colourless tube — drag the divider across its two baths:

before.label: ice water
before.text: The tube pales: dimerisation is exothermic, so removing heat pushes that direction, building the colourless dimer N₂O₄.

after.label: a heat bath
after.text: The tube darkens: added heat pushes the endothermic direction, making more of the choking brown NO₂.

config.why: No measurement kit needed: the balance point IS the shade you see. Cobalt mood mugs run the same trick — pink when cool, blue when hot.

activities.caption: call K from the settling curves
activities.name: eqKEstimate

config.prompt: Read the widget's settled mixture: roughly 0.33 units of product against 0.07 of reactant. What ratio is K?
config.why: The ratio lands far above 1, so the destination sits mostly with the products — a reaction that 'mostly goes'.
config.context: K far above 1 means the reaction goes; K far below 1 means it barely starts.

activities.anchor: stress a system at equilibrium and it shifts to oppose the stress
activities.caption: file each poke by where the balance runs
activities.name: eqLeChatSort

config.prompt: Three pokes, one silent case — file each by what the balance does:

items.label: add more ethanol to the ester balance
raise the pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (4 molecules → 2)
condense ammonia out of the loop
heat an exothermic synthesis like ammonia production
breathe fast and dump CO₂ from the blood buffer
squeeze the ester balance — 2 gas molecules on each side
add a catalyst to any settled system

config.why: Add reagent and it is consumed; squeeze and the side with fewer gas molecules wins; heat helps the endothermic direction; catalysts touch speed only.

activities.anchor: roughly half the nitrogen in your body passed through the Haber–Bosch process
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the one-line chemistry of ammonia
activities.name: eqHaberCloze

config.text: The Haber line is N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, exothermic with ΔH = %%0%% kJ/mol — and going from %%1%% gaseous molecules on the left to %%2%% on the right is why high pressure favours ammonia.
config.hint: The lesson quotes the enthalpy change directly; count the gas molecules on each side of the arrow.

activities.caption: slide to the temperature the plant actually runs at
activities.name: eqTempPlace

config.prompt: Ammonia synthesis is exothermic: cold buys yield, heat buys speed. Slide the marker to the temperature industry settles on.
config.why: 450 °C — under that mark the reaction crawls (the triple bond barely cracks); the yield sacrificed is recovered by condensing product out and recycling gas.

activities.caption: rebuild the plant loop — how 15% per pass becomes 97% overall
activities.name: eqLoopOrder

config.prompt: Put the industrial design loop in order:
items: Run N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ over an iron catalyst, 200 atm, at the settled temperature
Only about 15% converts each pass — the speed–yield trade-off
Condense the ammonia out of the loop, shifting the balance forward
Recirculate the unreacted N₂ and H₂ back through the beds
Overall conversion approaches 97% — the destination set, the road engineered
config.why: Equilibrium chemistry sets the destinations; kinetics and economics choose the road.

activities.anchor: This turns "which way will it go?" into arithmetic
activities.caption: pair each situation with its verdict
activities.name: eqQMatch

config.prompt: Pair each situation with its verdict:

pairs.left: heat added to an exothermic balance
pairs.right: K itself falls; the destination retreats

config.why: Same expression as K, any concentrations — the quotient makes predicting a shift pure calculation, and opens the ICE tables of the advanced tier.
